items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
CAO-EDI-26-001, 2025 Accessibility Status Report
notes:
Haley Gienow-McConnell, Accessibility Lead, provided a presentation. A copy of the presentation was attached to the agenda. The presentation and report is a legislated requirement as part of the AODA. Staff provided highlights of projects and priorities from the past year.

In response to questions from Committee, Amy Osika, Manager of Waterloo Region Housing, explained how the number of accessible units in new builds are determined by provincial guidelines. 

Committee expressed interest in an additional report on the potential future of the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee which would also include more information on how residents can be a part of the committee.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
PDL-CAS-26-003, Proposed Regional Procedural By-law
notes:
Tim Brubacher, Regional Clerk, provided an introduction to the report and an overview of the proposed housekeeping changes. 

In response to questions from Committee, T. Brubacher provided clarification that the proposed changes on delegates that are speaking on issues that are not on the agenda; the limit of 20 minutes is meant to save Council/Committee time.

T. Brubacher also elaborated on how unanimous consent is used for motions that are perfunctory. Committee was interested in this coming back in a future agenda.

Committee also expressed concern over reports going on the Addendum agenda and that more reports should go on the original agenda.

Committee also expressed interest in an amendment to changing the motion to extend to start at 10 p.m. instead of 11 p.m. Committee is also interested in seeing how many times the motion to extend has had to be used this Council term.

Committee inquired on potentially having Council meetings start earlier then 7 p.m.

Staff will further research inquires raised by Committee and are targeting a return to Committee/Council in April for enactment if the recommendation is passed later in March.

motions.item_title: Councillor C. Huinink Motion Re: Accessibility Standards
motions.text: WHEREAS over their lifespan most Ontarians will encounter some form of accessibility barriers in the built environment and the design of public spaces, AND WHEREAS the Ontario Building Code establishes only a minimum level of accessibility for buildings and therefore does not presently meet the accessibility needs of all people, AND WHEREAS accessibility in the built environment should be improved by integrating standards into the Code that promote meaningful access of buildings and sites for people with a range of accessibility requirements including vision, hearing, neurodiversity, and mobility, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT The Regional Municipality of Waterloo requests that the Province of Ontario incorporate the latest accessibility standards established by the Canadian Standards Association (CSA) into the Provincial Building Code to ensure that all new construction of public spaces in Ontario meets accessibility standards, and that the provincial government commits to achieving the Rick Hansen Foundation Accessibility Certification (RHFAC) gold certification on all its newly constructed buildings. And further that a copy of this motion be sent to: • The Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario • The Honourable Rob Flack, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing • Local and area MPs, MPPs and Heads of Council • The Association of Municipalities of Ontario • Ontario’s Big City Mayors and • Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS over their lifespan most Ontarians will encounter some form of accessibility barriers in the built environment and the design of public spaces,
AND WHEREAS the Ontario Building Code establishes only a minimum level of accessibility for buildings and therefore does not presently meet the accessibility needs of all people,
 
AND WHEREAS accessibility in the built environment should be improved by integrating standards into the Code that promote meaningful access of buildings and sites for people with a range of accessibility requirements including vision, hearing, neurodiversity, and mobility,
 
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT The Regional Municipality of Waterloo requests that the Province of Ontario incorporate the latest accessibility standards established by the Canadian Standards Association (CSA) into the Provincial Building Code to ensure that all new construction of public spaces in Ontario meets accessibility standards, and that the provincial government commits to achieving the Rick Hansen Foundation Accessibility Certification (RHFAC) gold certification on all its newly constructed buildings.

And further that a copy of this motion be sent to:
•    The Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario
•    The Honourable Rob Flack, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing
•    Local and area MPs, MPPs and Heads of Council
•    The Association of Municipalities of Ontario
•    Ontario’s Big City Mayors and
•    Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario
